name: Korney Korneevich and XOR (easy version)
description: This is an easier version of the problem with smaller constraints. Korney Korneevich dag up an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$. Korney Korneevich has recently read about the operation bitwise XOR , so he wished to experiment with it. For this purpose, he decided to find all integers $$$x \ge 0$$$ such that there exists an increasing subsequence of the array $$$a$$$, in which the bitwise XOR of numbers is equal to $$$x$$$. It didn't take a long time for Korney Korneevich to find all such $$$x$$$, and he wants to check his result. That's why he asked you to solve this problem! A sequence $$$s$$$ is a subsequence of a sequence $$$b$$$ if $$$s$$$ can be obtained from $$$b$$$ by deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements. A sequence $$$s_1, s_2, \ldots , s_m$$$ is called increasing if $$$s_1 \lt s_2 \lt \ldots \lt s_m$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 500$$$) — the elements of the array $$$a$$$.
output_specification: In the first line print a single integer $$$k$$$ — the number of found $$$x$$$ values. In the second line print $$$k$$$ integers in increasing order $$$x_1, x_2, \ldots x_k$$$ ($$$0 \le x_1 \lt \ldots \lt x_k$$$) — found $$$x$$$ values.
approach_summary: Define state dp[mask][i] capturing the subset of visited/chosen elements. Transition by iterating over valid unset bits in O(2^N × N) time.
